declared.how: a daily figure published by the provider in tokens

derived.how: a published request cap x 500 tokens a reply, or this model's published unit price divided into a published allowance; the arithmetic is in each row's volume_evidence

cerebras.evidence: Their pricing page on 2026-09-06 describes free access only as 'Free Trial: $5 in free credits after making an account' and publishes no daily free-tier ceiling at all. The numbers below are what the response headers of a free-trial key reported between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-07. They may be trial allowance rather than a standing free tier. Re-measure before relying on them. 1,000,000 tokens/day is the provider's own token figure (MEASURED). Read on a free trial key; may be that tier's allowance, not a standing free tier. Binding limit: 5 requests per minute. Two calls inside the same minute need roughly 13 s between them. Applies per ACCOUNT.

google.evidence: The public docs page no longer prints the per-model table; it points you at aistudio.google.com/rate-limit, which needs a login. The figures below were read off that console screen on 2026-09-06. Free tier means literally 'no billing account linked': linking one moves the project to Tier 1 and off these numbers. Because the limits are per PROJECT, a second API key in the same project buys you nothing. 500 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 250,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Requests per DAY on the Flash models: 500 a day on 3.5 Flash-Lite, and no daily figure has been read for 3.8 Flash. Applies per PROJECT.

kenari.evidence: Three tiers by account status. A new account is Solo: 50 free-model requests a day and 5 a minute. A top-up of Rp 10,000 moves it to Payer, at 1,000 a day. The header measured on 2026-09-07 read x-ratelimit-limit 5, which matches the Solo per-minute figure. 50 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 25,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. Binding limit: Fifty free requests a day until a top-up moves the account to Payer. Applies per ACCOUNT.

openrouter.evidence: The daily cap depends on lifetime credits purchased, and applies across ALL :free models combined, not per model. This condition is the one most lists drop, which makes their number wrong for a new account by a factor of twenty. What a NEW account gets; rises to 1,000/day under the conditions in LIMITS.md, and is shared across all free models. 50 requests/day (DECLARED) x 500 tokens a reply = 25,000 tokens/day. The request cap is the provider's figure; the token figure is arithmetic done here, so it is DERIVED, not DECLARED. rpd is tiered by lifetime credits purchased: see free_models_combined Applies per ACCOUNT.

xkiro.evidence: The largest confirmed free token allowance in this list by a wide margin, and it took one GET to find - it was sitting behind an endpoint nobody had asked. Requests per day are NOT published; the ceiling here is tokens. 5,000,000 tokens/day is the provider's own token figure (MEASURED). Binding limit: Tokens, not requests. 5M/day is roughly 3,500 pages of output, so on this provider you will hit model quality or latency long before you hit the quota. Applies per ACCOUNT.

promised.note: what the providers advertise, added up the way most lists add it. Not a measurement and never on the shelf: a per-minute ceiling is what a provider refuses to exceed in one minute, not a rate it will serve for 1,440 of them.

behind_payment.note: a real recurring quota that begins only after money changes hands. Free here means no money spent, so these figures are shown with their condition and are never ranked and never summed.

distance.ceilings_compared_as: the output ceiling where a split is published, the bare tpm where it is not; an input ceiling is never compared with the output target

meter.how: min(max_pace_rpm x max_tokens_per_call x 60, token_cap_per_run / cap_stop_min_minutes x 60)

burst.what: 30-second burst, per provider, latest reading; bench/throughput.py; a rate, never a day

ceilings_per_minute.note: Output-only and combined in+out ceilings are two shelves and are never added together; only the output-only shelf is compared with the output target.

grants.quote: Each model (such as qwen-plus, qwen3.6-plus, or qwen3.6-plus-2026-04-02) has its own independent free quota (typically 1,000,000 tokens). Quota cannot be merged or transferred across models.

one_time.note: true exactly once; never added to the daily shelf. A grant recorded per_model is per model, not multiplied by the models this list tracks.

grants.quote: Free accounts include a starter amount of usage for a smaller set of starter models. Instead, your included amount refreshes at each monthly reset.

drawn.caveat: drawn at a planned pace of 30 requests a minute and a realised 29.0 (624 launched over 22 minutes, at most 2 in flight) x 700 tokens a call: a floor for the hour measured, times 24, not their ceiling
drawn.note: alibaba drew 699,585 tokens in one measured hour on 2026-09-07. If that hour repeated 24 times it would be 16,790,040 a day, and nobody has measured that, so the figure is printed here and never added to the shelf. Drawn at a planned pace of 30 requests a minute and a realised 29.0 (624 launched over 22 minutes, at most 2 in flight) x 700 tokens a call: a floor for the hour measured, times 24, not their ceiling. The only free capacity here is a one-time grant of 1,000,000 tokens for this model, which at this rate lasts about 1.4 hours.

drawn.caveat: drawn at a planned pace of 5 requests a minute and a realised 2.2 (63 launched over 29 minutes, at most 2 in flight) x 700 tokens a call: a floor for the hour measured, times 24, not their ceiling
drawn.note: kenari drew 29,236 tokens in one measured hour on 2026-09-07. If that hour repeated 24 times it would be 701,664 a day, and nobody has measured that, so the figure is printed here and never added to the shelf. Drawn at a planned pace of 5 requests a minute and a realised 2.2 (63 launched over 29 minutes, at most 2 in flight) x 700 tokens a call: a floor for the hour measured, times 24, not their ceiling. kenari also publishes a DERIVED daily figure, and that is the one on the shelf.

note: defensible_tokens_per_day = MEASURED + DECLARED + DERIVED, largest figure per provider, and it is the only number the daily shelf and the distance use. PAID-PLAN, UNKNOWN and DRAWN are shown and never counted. A drawn hour is one measured hour: the day it would make if it repeated 24 times is printed with that condition and is never added. A quota that starts after a payment is not free capacity and is never added. Bursts and ceilings are per minute and are never multiplied out to a day. Money is never converted into tokens.
